title: Partially-Commutative Polynomial Optimization
authors: Abhishek Mishra, Moisés Bermejo Morán, Stefano Pironio
abstract: Semidefinite programming hierarchies for commutative and non-commutative polynomial optimization represent a powerful computational tool with many applications in quantum information. In such applications, a given variable is typically not either commuting or non-commuting with all other variables, but instead commutes with some variables and does not commute with others, i.e., the variables satisfy some partial commutation relations. While such partial commutation relations can always be incorporated in a fully non-commutative setting through suitable linear constraints in the semidefinite programming relaxations, exploiting their algebraic properties from the onset can result in more compact relaxations. This leads us to introduce partially-commutative polynomial optimization, a framework that encompasses commutative and non-commutative polynomial optimization, allowing for arbitrary commutation relations among the variables. We point out that the underlying algebraic structure is that of a partially-commutative monoid. We present and review several key aspects of such monoids and show how they can be used to build SDP relaxations for partially-commutative polynomial optimization problems in which the partial commutations are natively implemented in the monomial structure, without the need of additional linear constraints.
summary: This paper develops Partially-Commutative Polynomial Optimization (PCPO), a generalization for optimizing polynomials whose variables only partially commute. It achieves this by constructing compact Semidefinite Programming relaxations that natively encode these partial commutation relations into the monomial structure, offering a significant computational improvement over methods relying solely on linear constraints.
main_problem: The paper addresses Partially-Commutative Polynomial Optimization (PCPO), a generalization of standard commutative and non-commutative optimization problems.
main_result: It introduces PCPO, which models systems where variables exhibit partial commutation relations, and shows that these can be incorporated into compact Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations by exploiting the underlying partially-commutative monoid structure.
method: The core method involves using SDP hierarchies derived from moment matrix theory, but crucially modifies the basis construction to natively implement partial commutation relations algebraically rather than through simple linear constraints.
model_or_system: The framework is motivated by quantum information scenarios involving multiple parties acting on shared systems, where operators exhibit selective commutation (partial commutations). This interpolates between fully commutative and fully non-commutative regimes.
key_observables: Optimization of polynomials over partially-commuting variables; the objective value $\langle\psi, p(A)\psiangle$ in the tracial setting.
important_parameters: The degree $d$ of the SDP relaxation hierarchy; the specific set of partial commutation relations defining the monoid structure.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that the algebraic properties derived from the partially-commutative monoid can be used to construct a reduced monomial basis for the SDP, avoiding the computational difficulties associated with general quotient algebra representations.
paper_structure: The paper reviews standard Non-Commutative Polynomial Optimization (NCPO) using NPA hierarchies before introducing PCPO. It focuses on adapting techniques from partially-commutative monoids to build efficient, constraint-free SDP relaxations for the general case.
why_interesting: For theorists working on open quantum systems or quantum information, this provides a powerful mathematical tool to analyze complex physical models (like multi-party entanglement measures) where operators do not commute fully but obey specific partial commutation rules.
